description: I’m a Computer Science student interested in AI and web development. I enjoy building projects and learning new things in a team. We’re looking for teammates who know Python, machine learning, frontend, or design. Beginners are welcome too. Let’s build something great together for NASA Space Apps!
summary: MedOrbit is an onboard health-monitoring and crew-care web app for astronauts. Each crew member signs in to a private portal, completes a guided four-step daily check-in (mood, sleep, vitals, symptoms), and sees their readings on an interactive 3D anatomical body where flagged organs light up. MedOrbit compares every signal against both Earth-standard and space-adapted limits based on NASA Human Research Program risks such as neck-vein flow changes, optic-nerve swelling (SANS), bone loss and radiation. It pulls live space weather from NASA's DONKI API, reads real heart-rate and SpO₂ data from a smartwatch through Apple Health, and offers "Orbit", an AI companion that explains a crew member's own records in plain words without diagnosing. The medical officer sees the whole crew, while mission control sees only what the crew sends. On long missions with communication delays, crews must manage their own health; MedOrbit gives them early, private, clear decision support.
details:
What it does: Private astronaut portals with a 4-step daily check-in; a personal dashboard (vitals, check-in history, alerts); an interactive X-ray-style 3D body where clicking an organ shows its colour and values; every signal judged by Earth rules and space-adapted rules side by side, based on NASA HRP risks; live NASA DONKI space weather; real smartwatch data (Ronin R-012 → Apple Health → MedOrbit); the "Orbit" AI companion with medical safety rules; guided breathing and a private journal; WhatsApp-style messages with the flight surgeon and mission control; role-based privacy (each astronaut sees only their own data, the medical officer sees the crew).
Benefits & impact: Earlier warning of space-specific health risks and more crew autonomy, which matters for Moon and Mars missions where Earth replies take minutes.
Tools: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js / React Three Fiber, Recharts, SQLite, Groq LLM API, NASA DONKI API, Apple Health + iOS Shortcuts, Ronin R-012 smartwatch, Vercel, GitHub.
Creativity: Dual Earth-vs-space rule comparison, a clickable 3D anatomy, real wearable data and live NASA space weather in one view, and an AI companion that explains but never diagnoses.
Factors considered: Crew privacy and consent, communication delay, accessibility, phone and laptop layouts, and that this is decision support, not diagnosis.
